title: The Celebrated Jumping Frog
summary: Jim Smiley trains a special jumping frog, but a stranger makes a secret plan.

sentences.text: It was a heavy, languid afternoon in the decaying mining camp when an old man with a famously exhaustive memory cornered me.
His name was Simon Wheeler, and he possessed the tranquil gravity of a man who believed every trivial detail of existence deserved a solemn chronicle.
Settling beside me with a worn pipe, he began to unspool the endless history of a fellow named Jim Smiley.
To hear Wheeler tell it, Smiley was a man whose entire philosophy of life could be summarized in a single, compulsive urge to gamble.
No sooner had the old man set the scene than he launched into illustrations of Smiley's staggering audacity.
If a stray dog was trotting down the dusty street, Smiley would immediately wager on which direction it might turn or which animal was faster.
Nowhere was his obsession more pronounced than in his treatment of ordinary domestic fowl and livestock.
Should two ordinary birds happen to alight upon a rustic fence rail, Smiley would quietly calculate the odds and bet on which one would take flight first.
He would follow a parson to church, wagering on whether the man would take the high road or the low.
If the local minister fell gravely ill, Smiley would immediately bet on whether he would recover or pass away.
People knew him intimately because his bets were always ready in his pocket, waiting for any conceivable event to unfold.
Not a soul in the settlement could ever dissuade him from discovering a fresh challenge every single day.
The man practically lived for the electric thrill of competition and the modest satisfaction of winning cash from his neighbors.
His ambition was not merely financial, but aesthetic; he craved the tactical supremacy of being right.
Smiley once spent three months training a common bull pup, affectionately naming him Andrew Jackson, to fight anything that barked.
Yet his masterpiece, the crowning achievement of his betting career, was an entirely different sort of athlete.
Smiley managed to capture a modest, unassuming frog from a nearby marsh and brought him back to his quarters.
With infinite patience, he christened the creature Dan'l Webster and resolved to transform him into a sporting legend.
He trained that remarkably focused creature every single day until it could effortlessly out-jump any other amphibian in the county.
Dan'l Webster possessed a peculiar athletic gift, and his vertical propulsion could reach heights that astonished even experienced local observers.
Smiley was immensely proud of his champion jumper, guarding him jealously and keeping him confined in a small lattice box.
Under a strict regimen of education, the little creature grew noticeably stronger with every single practice session.
Smiley spent countless hours working with the animal to ensure absolute success in every scheduled contest.
He would catch a fly, release it just above the box, and watch with profound admiration as the frog launched itself like a miniature cannonball.
Every single person in the region knew about the famous jumper and spoke of his astonishing athletic feats with hushed reverence.
The animal eventually became a powerful symbol of civic pride for its enthusiastic owner.
Many curious travelers came from far away just to witness the jumping frog perform its legendary aerial acrobatics.
Smiley would sit on his porch, holding the box, waiting for anyone foolish enough to doubt his champion.
It seemed nothing could disrupt his steady accumulation of local prestige and occasional silver coins.
His faith in Dan'l Webster was absolute, unshakable, and entirely devoid of reasonable doubt.
One particularly warm afternoon, a stranger with a smooth face and calculating eyes walked past Smiley's cabin.
Smiley intercepted the traveler, thrust the small box into his hands, and casually remarked that Dan'l was the finest jumper in the whole country.
The stranger carefully examined the humble box, lifted the lid, and looked down at the quiet amphibian with a neutral expression.
He poked the creature gently, but he did not outwardly believe the extravagant story the proud owner was spinning.
After a long moment of deliberate silence, the stranger finally stated that he would gladly accept a wager if Smiley could provide a suitable competitor.
He looked at the box with deep, analytical interest, quietly weighing his strategic options.
The traveler desperately wanted to win the game by any means possible, driven by a cold desire to outwit the local champion.
Noticing the stranger hesitation, Smiley smiled broadly and accepted the challenge without a single moment of doubt.
He felt entirely certain that his undefeated champion would triumph once again and humiliate the newcomer.
The stranger waited patiently on the porch while pretending to ponder his master plan for the upcoming race.
He asked Smiley to hold his own box for a moment while he walked down to the swamp to find a rival frog.
Smiley readily agreed, completely unaware of the malicious strategy forming behind those calm eyes.
Smiley went off down the muddy, wet road with high hopes, eager to catch a fresh animal for the stranger.
While Smiley was away, the stranger executed his secret, calculated plan to secure the money by dishonest means.
He reached into the lattice box, lifted poor Dan'l Webster out by his slippery legs, and held the creature firmly in his palm.
Pulling a small bag of heavy lead shot from his pocket, the stranger forced the metal pellets down the frog throat.
He filled the poor animal completely with heavy lead shot until the creature was packed tightly from chest to belly.
When the difficult work was finished, the stranger put the heavy creature back inside the box and waited quietly.
The metal made the animal extraordinarily heavy and utterly unable to move its muscular legs properly.
The stranger knew that his own newly caught frog would easily win the race now against such a disabled opponent.
He sat back on the wooden bench, waiting calmly for Smiley to return with the fresh competitor.
The secret plan was fully complete, neatly executed, and completely hidden from casual view.
Nothing could stop the cunning stranger from taking the cash and walking away victorious.
He suppressed a smug grin as the sound of Smiley boots echoed up the muddy path.
Smiley soon returned, carrying a modest green frog in his hand, and immediately handed the race over to the stranger.
Both animals were placed side by side upon the dry ground to start the big competition.
Smiley shouted the signal, and the stranger's animal leaped away immediately in a powerful arc.
Poor Dan'l, however, could not move an inch from his starting position.
Weighed down by the heavy metal inside, the exhausted animal only gave a sad, pathetic little shake of its head.
Smiley watched the entire scene with total surprise, profound shock, and lingering confusion.
He could not understand for the life of him why his once invincible champion had suddenly failed to jump.
The fresh animal crossed the finish line with ease while Dan'l stayed firmly anchored to the ground.
The race was over in a matter of seconds, leaving Smiley staring down in sheer disbelief.
The stranger collected the money immediately and walked away with a triumphant smile on his face.
Only after the man had vanished down the road did a deeply confused Smiley finally discover the heavy trick.
He bent down, picked up the strange creature, and suddenly realized why the crucial jump had failed so miserably.
Although he tried to run after the smart stranger, the dishonest man was already far away and out of sight.
Smiley pried the animal open and found the hidden lead shot rolling out onto the wooden floor.
He finally understood that he had been ruthlessly tricked by an opponent who played a dishonest game.
The old man Wheeler paused here, looking at me with a steady gaze to ensure I grasped the moral of the lengthy narrative.
He told me this story simply to illustrate how rapidly fortunes can change when someone relies on deception.
Life, according to Wheeler, is full of strange events that teach us unforgettable lessons about human nature.
